facts.text: Notification No. 638 dated May 25, 1937 was issued by the respondent State of Madras under clause b of sub-section 5 of s.65A of the Hindu Religious Endowments Act, 1926 (Madras Act II of 1927), declaring the Sri Thiyagarajaswami Temple and its endowments subject to Chapter VI-A.

facts.text: The appellant Sri-la-Sri Subramania Desika Gnana Sambanda Pandarasannadhi is the Hereditary Trustee of the Rajan Kattalai of Sri Thiyagarajaswami Temple.

anchor.surface_text: declaring that the temple in question and the specific endowments attached thereto shall be subject to the provisions of Chapter VI-A of the said Act. facts.text: Sri Thiyagarajaswami Temple is located in Tiruvarur, Thanjavur District.

anchor.surface_text: In the town of Tiruvarur in Thanjavur Dist. there is an ancient temple. The Presiding Deity is Sri Thyagarajaswami.

facts.text: Sri Thiyagarajaswami Temple is an ancient temple with Presiding Deity Sri Thyagarajaswami.

anchor.surface_text: In the town of Tiruvarur in Thanjavur Dist. there is an ancient temple. The Presiding Deity is Sri Thyagarajaswami.

facts.text: The temple has a large number of specific endowments called Kattalais for special services, festivities, and charities.

anchor.surface_text: A distinguishing feature of this temple is that apart from an allowance called the Mohini allowance, there is numberother property which can be treated as devoted for its general maintenance. A large number of specific endowments called Kattalais with specific reference to special services in the temple, its festivities and several charities in glorification of the principal deity, have however been made in respect of this temple.

facts.text: There are 13 Kattalais in the temple, including Rajan Kattalai, Ulthurai Kattalai, Abisheka Kattalai, and Annadanam Kattalai.

anchor.surface_text: It is said that there are 13 such Kattalais, the important amongst them being Rajan Kattalai, Ulthurai Kattalai, Abisheka Kattalai and Annadanam Kattalai.

facts.text: Endowments for Kattalais were made by Indian Rulers who ruled Thanjavur before British Rule.

anchor.surface_text: In respect of these Kattalais, large endowments have been made. According to the appellant, these endowments were made by the Indian Rulers who ruled Thanjavur before the establishment of the British Rule.

facts.text: Management of each Kattalai is vested in a certain Trustee or Trustees hereditarily.

anchor.surface_text: It appears that the management of each one of these Kattalais is vested in a certain Trustee or Trustees hereditarily.

facts.text: Trusteeship of Rajan Kattalai vests in the head of Dharmapuram mutt in Thanjavur district.

anchor.surface_text: The trusteeship of Rajan Kattalai vests in the head of the Dharmapuram mutt in the Thanjavur district.

facts.text: Dharmapuram mutt has large endowments of lands in Thanjavur and Tirunelveli districts and manages about 27 temples.

anchor.surface_text: The Dharmapuram mutt itself has large endowments of lands in Thanjavur and Tirunelveli districts. The head of this mutt is known as Pandarasannadhi and under his management there are about 27 temples.

facts.text: Head of Dharmapuram mutt appoints deputies to manage temples, including Kattalai Thambiran for Rajan Kattalai services.

anchor.surface_text: Having regard to the nature of the duties of the head of a mutt of this importance and magnitude, it is number possible for the Pandarasannadhi to supervise all the temples personally, and so, Deputies are appointed on his behalf to supervise and look after the management of the various institutions. With regard to the services companynected with the Rajan Kattalai in Sri Thyagarajaswami temple at Thiruvarur, the head of Dharmapuram mutt generally functions through a deputy known as Kattalai Thambiran.

facts.text: In 1910, a suit was filed under s.92 CPC in Sub-Court at Thanjavur for settlement of a scheme to manage the temple affairs.

anchor.surface_text: As a result. in 1910, a suit was flied under s.92 of the Code of Civil Procedure for the settlement of a scheme to manage the affairs of the temple in the Sub-Court at Thanjavur.

facts.text: A scheme was settled by Sub-Court Thanjavur and substantially confirmed by Madras High Court in Gnana Sambanda v. Vaithilinga Mudaliar.

facts.text: In Ramanathan Chettiar v. Balayee Ammal, Madras High Court held that Kattalais are appendages of the temple with no private ownership.
